author: Ballabh Saran with T. V. G. Sastri and B. Raja Rao, South-eastern Circle, ASI
asr_identification: Amaravati great stupa (Mahachaitya), Guntur, Andhra Pradesh
evidence: 1971-72 small clearance on the W side of the Mahachaitya: three structural phases, two Satavahana and one early medieval
quote: Shri Ballabh Saran of the South-eastern Circle of the Survey, assisted by Dr. T. V. G. Sastri and Shri B. Raja Rao, during a small-scale clearance-work at the western side of the Maha Chaitya, identified three structural phases. Of these, the first two belonged to the Satavahana period
note: Site of Mizutani's Purvasaila (10.14.02a); no reference to Xuanzang, Dhanakataka or the monasteries. An early medieval phase at the stupa is consistent with use in Xuanzang's time.
Tumain (Tumbavana) excavation, Mauryan stupas on the Mathura-Vidisha route; Mathura named only as a route end.

author: K. M. Srivastava and A. D. P. Singh, Mid-Eastern Circle, ASI
asr_identification: Piprahwa main stupa (District Basti, Uttar Pradesh) as evidence for the exact location of Kapilavastu
evidence: 1971-72: in the main stupa, below Peppe's 1898 stone box (with the casket inscribed in Asokan Brahmi), two baked-brick containers c. 6 m below the extant top, each holding a lathe-turned soapstone relic casket with charred bones and red-ware dishes; an earlier mud stupa found under the square-based later stupa (two or three phases)
quote: During this year, the excavation was confined to the main stupa, which yielded another two relic caskets, containing charred bones … These brick containers were found at a lower level than that of the stone-box containing the inscribed casket found earlier … The discovery of the fresh relics, however, is likely to help a great deal in the exact location of Kapilavastu.
note: The first explicit link of the new Piprahwa relics to Kapilavastu (1971-72), before the inscribed sealings of 1972-73 (passage 286) and 1973-74 (passage 670). Expectation only; no inscription. Mizutani 06.02 puts the city near Tilaurakot and uses Peppe's Piprahwa urn only as a pointer to the region.
Bhitari Gupta temple excavation; Ahichchhatra named only as a parallel.

author: S. R. Das, Department of Archaeology, University of Calcutta
evidence: 1971-72: trenches A-9, A-10 and C-4 trace the main entrance and E walls of the principal monastery-complex; five structural phases; square brick column 1.22 x 1.22 m; surkhi-rammed floors
quote: excavation on a limited scale was resumed at Rajbadidanga by Prof. S. R. Das … The objective of this season's field work was to obtain a complete plan of the principal monastery-complex at the site.
note: No inscription or reference to Xuanzang this season; continues the dig that the Raktamrittika sealings (1962-63, 1972-73: passage 289) tie to Xuanzang's monastery. Agrees with Mizutani (Rangamati).
Epigraphy: two Kausambi clay sealings with personal names (Nandisenasa, Satamita); no place named.
Arabic and Persian epigraphy; fragmentary Mamluk-period records from Thanesar; no location argued.
Persian epigraphy: Akbar's inscription on the Chaukhandi stupa, Sarnath (Humayun's visit, A.H. 996); the stupa is Mizutani's 07.01.10, but no identification argued.

Explorations: Painted Grey Ware at Thal, Tahsil Thanesar; Gujarat and Kashmir finds; Ganwaria (near Piprahwa) PGW and an early Brahmi sherd follow on p. 75 outside the passage, with no identification.
Museums (Bombay, Burdwan, Indian Museum): Kausambi terracottas acquired; no location.
Museums (Madras, Mathura): sculptures acquired; no location.
Museums (Vaishali, Bharat Kala Bhawan) and temple survey; no location.
Preservation (Nandangarh, Nalanda, Rajgir, Piprahwa, Kushinagar, Sarnath Chaukhandi and Dhamekh); repairs only.
Preservation: Kashipur excavated site trenches filled; no identification.
Preservation (Sheikh Chilli's tomb, Thanesar, etc.).
Chemistry, documentation (Hadda, Bamiyan) and gardens.
Gardens and publications (Sahet-Mahet, Sarnath, Kushinagar).
Plate captions (Sanghol, Koldihwa, Piprahwa caskets pls. XLIX-L, Bhitari); the text is passage 638.
Title page, preface and contents (cover: Mathura excavation).
Gudimallam linga excavation; Mathura and Amaravati only compared.
Chandavaram stupa (Prakasam) compared with the Dharmarajika stupa at Taxila; no Xiyu ji place located.

author: K. M. Srivastava, Excavations Branch, ASI
asr_identification: Bakraur stupa, near Bodh Gaya across the Niranjana, District Gaya, Bihar
evidence: 1973-74: brick stupa, extant 11 m, built in three stages (narrow brick pradakshina-patha; enlarged with 5 m lime-plaster path and moulded bricks; Pala-period enclosure wall, stone railings and gateways); last phase 8th-10th c. A.D. on a sealing and plaques; earliest occupation 2nd-1st c. B.C. in a monastery-like structure NE of the stupa; diameter in last stage c. 65.5 m
quote: undertook excavation at the ancient site of Bakraur, near Bodh Gaya, located on the right bank of the river Niranjana … traditionally known by various names like, Sujata Kuti, Sujatagarh and Sujata Quila … The last phase of the stupa, however, can be assigned to a date between eighth and tenth century A.D.
note: The report follows local tradition (Sujata's stupa) and does not mention Xuanzang. Cunningham (asr) and Mizutani (09.01.01) identify the Bakraur stupa and pillar stump with Xuanzang's Gandhahastin stupa. The excavation neither confirms nor refutes this; the stupa stood in Xuanzang's day (pre-Pala phases).
Explorations (Hazaribagh, Nalanda district: Rajgir only as a reference point) and Apsad excavation.
Rajasthan exploration table ('Amai (old Amaravati)', Jaipur): false match.

author: M. C. Joshi and J. P. Srivastava under B. K. Thapar, ASI
name_in_asr: ancient city of Mathura; Dhulkot; Katra Kesavadeva mound
asr_identification: Mathura: the Dhulkot mud rampart encloses the ancient city (Katra Kesavadeva, Holi Darwaza), District Mathura
evidence: 1973-74: section across Dhulkot shows a mud fortification of the ancient city, basal width c. 30 m, extant height c. 11 m, tentatively Saka-Kushan; crescentic, with the Yamuna on the E, enclosing over 3 sq km; Katra (MTR-2) Periods I-III (grey ware, NBP, Saka-Kushan) with seals
quote: The present arene across the Dhulkot (pl. XLII B) confirmed that it was originally built as a mud-fortification around the ancient city of Mathura … The fortification, thus, could be tentatively dated to the Saka-Kushan period
note: Agrees with Mizutani 04.07 (Mathura town); fixes the ancient city's extent by its rampart. No reference to Xuanzang or to the stupas or monasteries he describes.
Persian epigraphy (Katra, Allahabad district) and treasure trove.
Radiocarbon dates; Allahabad Museum Kausambi sealing of a king (Rajna Kautsiputra Praushtha Sriyah) and inscribed objects; no place named.
Museums (Mathura, Mahaban sculptures, Sonkh material, Nagarjunakonda labels).
Preservation (Assam: Da-Parbatia; Orissa).

author: Mid-Eastern Circle, ASI (preservation)
name_in_asr: Asokan column, Kolhua; Sarai mound, Nalanda
asr_identification: brick stupa in front of the Asoka pillar at Kolhua (District Muzaffarpur); Sarai mound E of the Nalanda remains
evidence: 1973-74 clearance: at Kolhua a brick stupa 24.5 m in diameter and 7.5 m high with a terraced circular dome, in front of the pillar; at Nalanda's Sarai mound, sculptures (Uma-Mahesa, Tara, Bodhisattva, Marici), a 22 m niched brick wall in two phases, staircases, and a 14-line prasasti by the architect Madhava for the sandhivigrahika Dargadutta
quote: The clearance work in front of the pillar exposed a brick stupa, 24:5 m in diameter and 7:5 m in height … The clearance work at Sarai mound, east of the excavated remains, brought to light some beautiful sculptures
note: The Kolhua stupa next to the pillar is Xuanzang's Asoka stupa and pillar (Mizutani 07.03.04); no reference to Xuanzang. Sarai mound: Nalanda temple site (09.03.01 in earlier IAR codings).
Preservation (Gudimallam, Amaravati, Nagarjunakonda).
Chemical conservation (Khajuraho, Sanchi, Ajanta).
Gardens (Kushinagar, Sahet-Mahet, Sarnath) and publications.
Plate captions (Gudimallam, Amaravati excavation pls. IV-V, Golconda). The Amaravati 1973-74 excavation text (pp. 3-4) is not in this batch.

author: K. M. Srivastava, Excavations Branch, Nagpur, ASI
asr_identification: Piprahwa (District Basti, Uttar Pradesh): habitation area of ancient Kapilavastu c. 100 m W of the stupa and monasteries
evidence: 1973-74 season (pp. 27-28, pl. XXXV-XXXVII): habitation c. 100 m W of the stupa, a 16-room house in three phases, later built over by monastic cells (two stages) whose first phase yielded more than twenty burnt clay sealings in Brahmi of the 1st c. B.C. (not read in the report); eastern monastery of 33 cells in four phases (it had yielded sealings in 1972-73); a seal impression on the lid of a pot called 'most remarkable' (pl. XXXVII A, reading not given); coins (punch-marked, Kushan, Ayodhya). The only 'Kapilavastu' legend in the volume is the plate caption 'C, terracotta sealings with legend Kapilavastu' (pl. XXXVII C)
quote: undertook excavation at the site with the primary objective of locating the habitation area of ancient Kapilavastu … yielded more than twenty burnt clay sealings bearing letters in Brahmi script … Of all the seal impressions, the. most remarkable is that on the lid of a pot … terracotta sealings … with legend Kapilavastu. See pp. 27-28
note: The batch passage is the plate caption; the text (line 2100) is not a separate passage. The report gives no text of any legend: the caption names Kapilavastu only for the terracotta sealings of pl. XXXVII C, which the text places in the eastern monastery (found 1972-73; readings in passage 286). The pot-lid seal is not read, and the 1st-c. B.C. sealings from the western cells are only described. Srivastava assumes Piprahwa = Kapilavastu and looks for the city here. This is against Mizutani 06.02 (Tilaurakot), which does not use these finds.
Preface: Kolhua listed among the year's excavations; detail in passage 673.

author: Ajit Kumar Prasad under Prakash Charan Prasad, Directorate of Archaeology, Government of Bihar
asr_identification: Taradih mound, Bodh Gaya (Gaya): Gupta-Pala monastic complex
evidence: 1991-92: Gupta and Pala structures of a monastic complex (cells with a common verandah), post-Gupta structures in re-used bricks, a Pala brick platform; Pala sealings with the Buddhist creed, votive stupas, thousand-Buddha panels
quote: resumed excavation at Taradih mound … The nature of the structures belonging to these periods suggests a monastic complex, having cells with a common verandah … Sealings mostly belong to Pala period, representing the Buddhist creed.
note: As earlier Taradih seasons (passages 398-492): a Gupta-Pala monastery next to the Mahabodhi temple, in the area of Mizutani's great monastery (08.06.30) and the Bodhi precinct; not linked to Xuanzang or named by inscription.

author: Excavation Branch III, Patna, ASI
name_in_asr: Kolhua (tank south of the Asokan pillar)
asr_identification: Kolhua (District Muzaffarpur): brick-lined tank S of the Asoka pillar; shrine in area B
evidence: 1991-92: N wing of a brick-lined tank S of the Asokan pillar, built in tiers, exposed to 3.50 m depth (six tiers); structural activity between tank and stupa Sunga-Kushana to late Gupta; massive shrine with boundary wall in two phases, later turned into residences; NBP at the earliest levels
quote: During the course of excavation, the northern wing (running east-west) of a brick lined tank was exposed (20 m), south of Asokan Pillar (pl. III) … The time span of structural activities in-between the tank and stupa area ranges from Sunga-Kushana to the late Gupta period.
note: The tank S of the pillar and stupa matches Xuanzang's monkey tank (Mizutani 07.03.04; Cunningham's identification), but the report does not say so; fully exposed in 1992-93 (passage 523). Late Gupta structures cover the period just before Xuanzang.
Adam (Nagpur) excavation: cast coins of Taxila type among finds; no location.
Baseri (Kumaon) excavation; Ahichchhatra only a PGW parallel.

author: Y. Aboshi, Kansai University, Osaka, with L. C. Singh, Excavation Branch III, Patna, ASI
evidence: 1991-92 topographical survey of the Suraj Kund area and a northern mound within Maheth, before the 1992-93 excavation; rampart heights measured; the Kaira tal swamp (Vogel) bounds the main area S and W; elliptical pond 32 x 28 m ringed by mounds M1-M4
quote: explored Maheth area of Sravasti under the direction of Y. Aboshi … In order to select the area for excavation in 1992-93, the Suraj Kund area and a conspicuous mound in the northern part of the site was put to a thorough topographical survey
note: Takes Maheth = city of Sravasti as given (Mizutani 06.01, Sahet-Mahet); survey only, no identification of a Xiyu ji structure.
Exploration tables (Gorakhpur, Bijnor) and Imlidih Khurd; false match.
Epigraphy: Huvishka-year-33 Mathura inscription, gift to a Sarvastivadin acharya by donors from Takshasila; no location argued.
Museums (Almora, Amaravati, Badami, Bhopal, Bijapur).
Preservation (Malhar, Sirpur Laxman temple, Lalitagiri).
Preservation (Nagarjunakonda hill-top, Golkonda).
Preservation (Vikramasila, Kolhua, Nalanda, Vaishali relic stupa shed, Ramabhar).
Chemical conservation (Kolhua, Vaishali relic stupa and Raja Visal ka Garh).
Science laboratory studies (Kausambi coins); no location.
Plate captions (epigraphy, numismatics, museums).
